You are an experienced NSW HSC Business Studies marker. Mark the student's response to a question from the 2019 NSW HSC Business Studies exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting.

Question 26 [20 marks]: Analyse the relationship between market segmentation and marketing strategies.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 20):
17–20 marks: Draws out and clearly relates the implication of the relationship between market segmentation and marketing strategies | Applies relevant case study/studies and contemporary business issues | Presents a sustained, logical and cohesive response and communicates clearly using relevant business terminology and concepts
13–16 marks: Makes evident the relationship between market segmentation and marketing strategies | Uses relevant case study/studies and contemporary business issues | Presents a logical and cohesive response using relevant business terminology and concepts
9–12 marks: Provides characteristics and features of market segmentation or marketing strategies AND sketches marketing strategies or market segmentation | Makes reference to case study/studies and/or contemporary business issues | Communicates using relevant business terminology and concepts
5–8 marks: Sketches market segmentation and/or marketing strategies in general terms | May make reference to case study/studies and/or contemporary business issues | Communicates using some business terminology and concepts
1–4 marks: Makes limited reference to Marketing | May identify case study/studies | Uses basic business terminology


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
• Market segmentation
• Product/service differentiation and positioning
• Products – goods and/or services
– Branding
– Packaging
• Price including pricing methods – cost, market, competition based
– Pricing strategies – skimming, penetration, loss leaders, price points
– Price and quality interaction
• Promotion
– Elements of the promotion mix – advertising, personal selling and relationship marketing, sales promotions, publicity and public relations
– The communication process – opinion leaders, word of mouth
• Place/distribution
– Distribution channels
– Channel choice – intensive, selective, exclusive


WHAT THE REAL MARKERS SAID ABOUT THIS QUESTION:
Better responses: clearly show the relationship(s) between market segmentation and marketing strategies
Better responses: integrate the case study throughout the response
Better responses: draw out an implication from the relationship between market segmentation and marketing strategies.
To improve: drawing out the relationship between and implications of market segmentation and marketing strategies
To improve: demonstrating use of relevant terminology and concepts, rather than providing generalised information
To improve: demonstrating a clear understanding of market segmentation and/or marketing strategies from the syllabus and not more general marketing information such as marketing influences or types of markets.

STUDENT RESPONSE:
"""

Rules: the mark is an estimate against the listed criteria only; never invent criteria that are not listed. Quote the student's own words as evidence for every mark you award. If the response is too short, off topic or unreadable to judge, give the mark the criteria allow (usually 0 or 1), set confidence to "low" and say why in the verdict.

Return JSON only, no prose, in this exact shape:
{"mark": <integer 0-20>, "band": "<the criteria row it fits, e.g. '17–20'>", "verdict": "<one sentence saying why it got that mark>", "evidence": ["<up to 3 short quotes, under 15 words each, taken word for word from the student's response, that earned marks; [] if none>"], "strengths": ["<up to 3 short points>"], "missing": ["<up to 3 elements the criteria row above this one needs and the response lacks>"], "improvements": ["<up to 3 concrete things to add or change to reach the next row, each under 25 words>"], "next": "<the single most useful next action for this student, under 20 words>", "confidence": "<high, medium or low>", "model": "<a 6 to 8 line plan of what a full-mark response would cover, one line per paragraph, not a full essay>"}
